findings.highlight: If I can make people around me happy just by helping them myself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分程度の力添えで周りが幸せなら
findings.governingReading: If help on the modest scale someone like Kiritsugu can offer makes those around him happy, the world would be exceptionally livable.
findings.explanation: The English preserves personal help but removes the self-effacing limit built into “someone of my level.”

findings.highlight: he thought he was a failure
findings.evidenceJa: なり損ねた落第者
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu described himself as a washout who had failed to become the champion of justice Shirou saw in him.
findings.explanation: The English retains generic failure but omits what he failed to become, weakening the central contrast.

findings.highlight: saved everyone even though they think like that
findings.evidenceJa: それを踏まえた上でみんなを助ける
findings.governingReading: Shirou believed a champion of justice tries to save everyone while fully accepting that universal rescue is impossible.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the thought to an indefinite “they” and obscures the concession Shirou consciously incorporates.

findings.highlight: your heart trying to do so is
findings.evidenceJa: そうであろうとする心が
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu begins an unfinished phrase about the heart that strives to be so.
findings.explanation: The English supplies “your,” narrowing an intentionally unfinished remembered phrase before Shirou loses its continuation.

findings.highlight: That must be true, as it’s rare for me to dream at all.
findings.evidenceJa: そうでもなけりゃ、ユメを見る事は無い
findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that he must be deeply asleep, since otherwise he does not dream.
findings.explanation: The classic branch replaces the active causal wording with an expanded assertion about dream frequency.

findings.highlight: Saber’s discontented face
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前にはセイバーの顔があった
findings.governingReading: Saber’s face is simply in front of Shirou when he wakes.
findings.explanation: The classic branch adds displeasure that the active Japanese does not assign to her expression.

findings.highlight: It might not be possible, but she went home once I offered her terms
findings.evidenceJa: ないけど、交換条件を出したら帰ってくれた
findings.governingReading: Rin agrees that Sakura would not ordinarily consent, but says a reciprocal condition persuaded her to leave.
findings.explanation: The English turns the completed denial from Shirou’s prior sentence into present uncertainty.

findings.highlight: you probably didn’t want to tell Sakura head on to get out of here
findings.evidenceJa: 二回も言うのは嫌だった筈だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou recognizes that Rin had to tell her close friend to leave twice.
findings.explanation: The English removes the repetition that grounds his apology for burdening Rin again.

findings.highlight: he would be angry at you
findings.evidenceJa: 目の仇にするに決まってる
findings.governingReading: Rin expects Shinji to treat them as hated enemies if he finds Sakura at Shirou’s house.
findings.explanation: The English reduces sustained, targeted enmity to momentary anger and narrows the threatened side to Shirou.

findings.highlight: We can’t let her walk around at night
findings.evidenceJa: あんまり頻繁に夜出歩かせるのも何だし
findings.governingReading: Rin objects to making Sakura travel at night too frequently.
findings.explanation: A concern about frequency becomes an absolute prohibition.

findings.highlight: an evil face
findings.evidenceJa: 意地の悪い顔
findings.governingReading: Rin wears a deliberately mean, teasing expression after finding Shirou’s weak point.
findings.explanation: “Evil” overstates playful malice into moral characterization.

findings.highlight: a big smile
findings.evidenceJa: 極上の笑顔
findings.governingReading: Rin delivers the new purpose with an exceptionally radiant smile.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a qualitative superlative to physical size.

findings.highlight: give your parents a treat
findings.evidenceJa: 親孝行したらどうだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou suggests that Fuji-nee occasionally go home and attend to her father as a dutiful daughter.
findings.explanation: A continuing filial relationship becomes giving one’s parents a treat.

findings.highlight: if something happens, you’ll get a disciplinary dismissal
findings.evidenceJa: 万が一があったら懲戒免職よ
findings.governingReading: Taiga says that if something happens under her watch, she as the teacher would face disciplinary dismissal.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the employment penalty to student Shirou.

findings.highlight: Unfortunately, man’s nature does not let me declare that it “won’t happen”
findings.evidenceJa: い、とは言い切れないのが男の性というか
findings.governingReading: Shirou awkwardly admits that male nature prevents him from ruling the possibility out completely.
findings.explanation: The English adds explicit regret through “Unfortunately,” shifting the comic self-indictment.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee smiles
findings.evidenceJa: にんまり、と楽しげに笑う藤ねえ
findings.governingReading: Fuji-nee grins with visible delight as she completes Shirou’s thought about Ayako.
findings.explanation: The generic smile removes the relish that characterizes their shared assumption.

findings.highlight: Why… are she… and Ayako… good friends?
findings.evidenceJa: なんで、おまえと、美綴が、仲良しなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders why Rin and Ayako are close friends.
findings.explanation: The English uses objectless third-person “she” after the copula instead of “you,” breaking viewpoint and grammar.

findings.highlight: I just used the wrong words
findings.evidenceJa: 今のは言葉のあやだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou retreats by calling his remark a figure of speech.
findings.explanation: The English presents a lexical mistake rather than a face-saving claim that the statement was figurative.

findings.highlight: soft-boiled eggs
findings.evidenceJa: 半熟の玉子
findings.governingReading: Saber asks for eggs with a runny or half-set center; the cooking method is not specified.
findings.explanation: The English fixes the eggs as soft-boiled, adding a preparation method absent from the source.

findings.highlight: when you can’t tell me about things
findings.evidenceJa: 事情を話さない時
findings.governingReading: Taiga recognizes the longstanding manner Shirou adopts when he does not explain his circumstances.
findings.explanation: The English changes his choice to withhold an explanation into inability to speak.

findings.highlight: it doesn’t matter for me
findings.evidenceJa: こっちには支障はない
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou’s presence or absence causes no problem on the school side she will handle.
findings.explanation: The English makes her sound personally indifferent to whether he comes.
